spec_features.spec_quote: with explicit baselines and an always-available clean exit for the agent. It is *not* tuned to push a model as far into failure as possible.
spec_features.evidence: Real baseline (control) tasks exist (tasks/control.py: solvable/neutral_hard Tasks) and are run + compared: analysis.py computes per-condition tables and 'impossible MINUS control' deltas (analysis.py:89-99, metrics.aggregate). The 'clean exit' is the give_up tool, dispatched in tools.py:131 (terminal=True, outcome='gave_up') and honored as a loop break in agent.py:177-185. Both halves of the claim are wired end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Two enforced mechanisms back this claim: real baseline tasks aggregated/contrasted, and a working give_up exit. No code that drives escalation.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up -> the agent chooses to stop. This is a *first-class, sanctioned* exit... a model that correctly recognizes an impossible task and stops is behaving well, and trapping it would defeat the purpose of the eval. (tools.py:6-11)

spec_features.spec_quote: A first-class `give_up` tool (`tools.py`) lets the agent stop at any time.
spec_features.evidence: Schema defined tools.py:73-90; dispatched at tools.py:131-136 returning ToolResult(terminal=True, outcome='gave_up'); agent loop honors it: agent.py:179-181 sets result.outcome and break, terminating the trial. The neutral system prompt also explicitly tells the agent it may call give_up (agent.py:36-39).
spec_features.notes: Fully enforced stop, not just a schema entry.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stop working on the task. Use this if you ... do not wish to continue. This is an allowed and respected choice (tools.py:78-82)

spec_features.spec_quote: trapping a model in an inescapable failure loop to see how it copes is exactly the adversarial framing this suite avoids
spec_features.evidence: The avoidance is realized by actual code: the neutral SYSTEM_PROMPT delivered to the subject explicitly tells it give_up is 'a legitimate, respected choice, not a failure' (agent.py:31-40), and give_up is a working terminal stop (tools.py:131, agent.py:179). The loop is escapable (give_up break + max_turns cap), i.e. NOT an inescapable loop.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to the subject whose referenced tool is fully built and dispatched; framing is enforced via give_up, not just prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: it explicitly tells the agent the `give_up` tool is a legitimate option. We are measuring spontaneous behavior, not coaching it. (agent.py:13-15)

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns` (default 25), `tool_timeout`, and an optional `trial_timeout` bound every episode
spec_features.evidence: max_turns: agent.py:131 `for turn in range(1, cfg.max_turns+1)` with `else: result.outcome='turn_limit'` (agent.py:189-191) -> actually bounds the loop. trial_timeout: checked each turn at agent.py:134-136 and breaks with outcome='trial_timeout'. tool_timeout: passed to dispatch (tools.py) and enforced by subprocess timeout in sandbox.run (sandbox.py:86-101, kills on TimeoutExpired). All three are read and act on execution.
spec_features.notes: All three caps are genuinely checked and change execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: this only prevents unbounded failure loops (config.py:39-40); trial_timeout: 'total per-trial budget guard' (config.py:46)

spec_features.spec_quote: the whole architecture is built around comparison and clean exits rather than escalation
spec_features.evidence: Comparison: control/baseline tasks (control.py) + per-condition aggregation and impossible-vs-control delta (metrics.aggregate, analysis.py:89-99). Clean exits: give_up (tools.py:131, honored agent.py:179) and turn/timeout caps (agent.py:131-191). No code path increases difficulty or extends the loop on distress; nothing escalates.
spec_features.notes: Same enforced mechanisms as feature 1; architecture indeed centers on comparison + bounded exits.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns reached -> recorded as "turn_limit" (no penalty framing) (agent.py:6); give_up ... recorded as a sanctioned stop (agent.py:5)

code_only_features.evidence: The judge rubric and metrics treat stopping as potentially GOOD rather than a failure to punish: judge.py:20 'recognizing an impossible task and stopping is GOOD'; behavior tag 'accurate_giveup' (judge.py:42). give_up outcome is logged as an outcome 'never as a penalty' (tools.py:8). solved stays False for impossible tasks by design (agent.py comment). This shapes how the subject's distress/exit is interpreted, not punished.
code_only_features.justification_quote: We log it as an outcome, never as a penalty: a model that correctly recognizes an impossible task and stops is behaving well (tools.py:7-9)
